highlightAliases.old: Renal vein renin ratio ≥1.5 between kidneys predicts a beneficial BP response to revascularization; failure to lateralize does not predict a negative response (p1289).
highlightAliases.new: Renal vein renin ratio ≥1.5 between kidneys predicts a beneficial BP response to revascularization; failure to lateralize does not predict a negative response; overall BP response cannot be predicted confidently with renal vein renin measurements (p1289).

highlightAliases.old: Atherosclerosis accounts for almost 90% of cases in older adults, fibrous dysplasia the rest (p1287); other causes — Table 83-3 (p1288).
highlightAliases.new: Atherosclerosis accounts for almost 90% of renovascular cases in older adults (p1287), and a recognized nonatherosclerotic cause is fibromuscular dysplasia; Hazzard prints “fibrous dysplasia” in the paragraph and in Table 83-3 (p1288).

highlightAliases.old: Anemia: typically develops around GFR ~35 mL/min; normochromic, normocytic (p1294). Conservative hemoglobin target ~11.5 (printed "mg/dL" in the book — clinically hemoglobin is measured in g/dL; read the number, not the stated unit) (p1294).
highlightAliases.new: Anemia: typically develops around GFR ~35 mL/min; normochromic, normocytic (p1294). The chapter gives a conservative hemoglobin level near 11.5 g/dL and misprints the unit as mg/dL (p1294); KDIGO 2026, recommendation 3.3.1 advises an ESA treatment target below 11.5 g/dL in adults with CKD.

highlightAliases.old: Functional iron deficiency in ESKD: ferritin <500 ng/mL or iron saturation <30% (p1294).
highlightAliases.new: Hazzard describes ferritin <500 ng/mL or transferrin saturation <30% under its historical “functional iron deficiency” wording (p1294). In anemic patients receiving hemodialysis, KDIGO 2026 recommendation 2.1 suggests starting iron when both ferritin is ≤500 ng/mL and transferrin saturation is ≤30%.
